name: Maknadbai
title: One of those who divorced their foreign wives
summary: Maknadbai was an Israelite mentioned in the book of Ezra who was among those who had taken foreign (non-Israelite) wives during the time of exile. He was one of those who agreed to divorce his foreign wife as part of Ezra's reforms to restore the people's covenant faithfulness to God.

keyEvents.title: Listed among those with foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Maknadbai is mentioned in the list of Israelites who had taken foreign wives in violation of God's law, during Ezra's time after returning from exile in Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reform against mixed marriages
keyEvents.description: Ezra led a comprehensive reform requiring Israelite men who had married women from foreign nations to divorce them in order to preserve the people's purity and covenant faithfulness.

keyEvents.title: The people's confession and pledge
keyEvents.description: The people gathered, confessed their sins, and made a covenant to separate from their foreign wives and follow God's law.

keyEvents.title: Appointment of an investigative committee
keyEvents.description: Leaders were appointed to investigate the matter thoroughly, and they reviewed all cases of mixed marriages among the people.
